The bus factor

None of this is a people problem. It is a system problem, and systems can be fixed.

Every one of these is real. You have probably lived at least three of them. There is a backup. Somewhere. Probably. Deploys happen when someone drives to the site. Same project, different behavior, no way to compare. Changes have no author, no reason, no way back. There is no staging. There is only production. And everything depends on one person's memory. This is the diagnosis. The cure takes four days.

05

Management wants v2.0, built on the only copy

New dashboards, a silo detail view, packaging line support: a big job. The team starts building, on the same copy that production came from. Two weeks in: screens renamed, tags moved, nothing finished. Every save lands on the only copy. No branch. No fallback. Remember this picture. It is about to be 3 AM.

06

The plan: four days, four chapters

  1. Day 1 · Labs 01 + 02Foundations and the Git mindsetGit internals, branching strategies, pull requests, everyday workflows. The v2.0 plus hotfix week, done right.
  2. Day 2 · Labs 03 + 04Collaboration and automationLinters and validation as a safety net, GitHub Actions, self-hosted runners, the Ignition 8.3 file structure and the first file-based deploy.
  3. Day 3 · Lab 05Ignition-specific deploymentsImage-based deploys: project, config and modules baked into one versioned image, promoted from test to production.
  4. Day 4 · Labs 06 + 07Ignition in the real worldSecrets, database migrations, modules and JARs. Then Lab 07: multi-gateway deploys, the whole cohort on one shared repo.

Each day ends with the same map of Oatmakers. Watch it heal.

Mustry gets the call. We take the job. Four days, seven labs, one company to fix. Day 1: get the history and the branching right. The hotfix week, replayed calmly. Day 2: automate the checking. A robot reviews every change before a human does. Day 3: automate the shipping, the Ignition way. Day 4: promote through environments, fan out to all eight sites, and cap it off yourself.
